questions.q: What are the steps to execute: Create OU[cite: 1]?
questions.explanation: This procedure allows administrators to create a new Organizational Unit (OU) within Active Directory to logically structure and manage network objects.
questions.answer: Server Manager → Tools → Active Directory Users and Computers R-click Domain New → Organizational Unit → [Name it]. [cite: 2]

questions.q: What are the steps to execute: Add User to OU[cite: 3]?
questions.explanation: Users can be organized by dragging them directly from the default Users container and dropping them into the designated Organizational Unit (OU).
questions.answer: Click on Users → Drag the user → Drop into the OU. [cite: 4]

questions.q: What are the steps to execute: Create User[cite: 5]?
questions.explanation: This describes the standardized workflow for provisioning a new user account with secure credentials within Active Directory.
questions.answer: Server Manager → Tools → Active Directory Users and Computers → click Domain → R-click Users → New → User → Enter First name, Last name, and Logon name → Enter strong password. [cite: 6]

questions.q: What are the steps to execute: Create Group & Add User[cite: 7]?
questions.explanation: This method establishes a new security or distribution group and populates it by adding user accounts via the group's properties panel.
questions.answer: Server Manager → Tools → Active Directory Users and Computers → R-click Domain → R-click Users → New → Group → Give it a name → R-click Group → Properties → Members → Add. [cite: 8]

questions.q: What are the steps to execute: Join Client to Domain[cite: 9]?
questions.explanation: To connect a client machine to a managed domain, network system properties must be altered using valid administrator credentials for authentication.
questions.answer: R-click This Computer → Properties → Domain or Workgroup → Change Select Member of Domain → Enter domain name → Enter admin username & password. [cite: 10]

questions.q: What are the steps to execute: Disable USB (GPO)[cite: 11]?
questions.explanation: This Group Policy configuration enhances endpoint security by systematically denying read/write privileges to all forms of removable storage across domain machines.
questions.answer: Server Manager → Tools → Group Policy Management → R-click Domain → Create GPO → Name it usb-blocker → R-click usb-blocker → Edit → Computer Config → Policies → Administrative Templates → System → Removable Storage Access → All Removable Storage Access: Deny all → Enable → R-click Domain Link an existing GPO → Select usb-blocker. [cite: 12]

questions.q: What are the steps to execute: Desktop Wallpaper (GPO)[cite: 13]?
questions.explanation: Enforces a uniform desktop background environment for domain users via a User Configuration policy referencing a specific image source path.
questions.answer: Server Manager → Tools → Group Policy Management → R-click Domain → Create GPO → Name it wallpaper → R-click wallpaper → Edit → User Config → Policies → Administrative Templates → Desktop → Desktop Wallpaper → Enable → Enter path (\Server.jpg) → R-click Domain → Link an existing GPO → Select wallpaper. [cite: 14]

questions.q: What are the steps to execute: Remove Taskbar (GPO)[cite: 15]?
questions.explanation: Utilizes Group Policy settings targeting User Configurations to control interface layouts by locking or hiding the default Windows taskbar.
questions.answer: Server Manager → Tools → Group Policy Management → R-click Domain Create GPO → Name it remove-taskbar → R-click remove-taskbar → Edit → User Config → Policies → Administrative Templates → Start Menu and Taskbar → Hide or Lock Taskbar → Enable → R-click Domain → Link an existing GPO → Select remove-taskbar. [cite: 16]

questions.q: What are the steps to execute: Install Program (GPO)[cite: 17]?
questions.explanation: Automates the remote deployment of software packages targeting Computer Configurations across network clients upon system startup.
questions.answer: Server Manager → Tools → Group Policy Management → R-click Domain Create GPO → Name it soft-ins → R-click GPO → Edit→ Computer Config → Policies → Software Settings → Software Installation → R-click → New → Package → Browse office file from \Server.office → Select Assigned → OK → R-click Domain → Link an existing GPO → Select soft-ins. [cite: 18]
